page.title: Networking
page.desc: How programs talk across machines: the TCP/IP stack, sockets, HTTP and TLS, and the latency and failure modes that distributed systems inherit.
page.intro: How programs talk across machines: the TCP/IP stack, sockets, HTTP and TLS, and the latency and failure modes that distributed systems inherit.

synapses.text: Link, internet (IP), transport (TCP/UDP) and application (HTTP, DNS) layers each solve one problem; the stack is the most successful abstraction in computing.
The network is not reliable, latency is not zero, bandwidth is not infinite: Peter Deutsch's list from 1994 still describes most outages.

children.title: TCP/IP
children.desc: IP routes packets between hosts; TCP (Cerf and Kahn, 1974) turns them into a reliable ordered byte stream with a three-way handshake, retransmission and congestion control; UDP skips all of that.

children.title: HTTP
children.desc: The web's request/response protocol: HTTP/1.1 (1997) text over TCP, HTTP/2 (2015) multiplexed binary frames, HTTP/3 (2022) over QUIC on UDP; TLS underneath for https.
